waveItem: Wave 1, item 4 (B3-GEOMGAP vacuous-0 counties: Williamson, McLennan)
requestedBy: doc-repo-bd (cross-session message), following up on tonight's CAD join-miss fix (PR #382)
scopeBasis: READ-ONLY investigation only, per the request. No store writes, no record changes, no repo code changes in any repo. All reads via psql against CORTEX_DATABASE_URL (the neondb holding cad_property/txgio_parcel) with `SET default_transaction_read_only = on;` set at the start of every session.
question: For Williamson (land_value uniformly NULL on R-prefix accounts) and McLennan (land_acres uniformly NULL), is this a matched row correctly earning absent-verified today (B3-GEOMGAP's own predicate is just the wrong check for these counties), or a real CAD-ingest quirk silently losing real data?

williamson_48491.verdict: REAL INGEST GAP, not a legitimate absence.
williamson_48491.liveQuery: WITH latest AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (prop_id) * FROM cad_property WHERE county_fips='48491' ORDER BY prop_id, tax_year DESC) SELECT (prop_id LIKE 'R%') AS is_r, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE land_value IS NULL), count(*) FILTER (WHERE land_acres=0) FROM latest GROUP BY 1;
williamson_48491.measured: 282,569 R-prefix accounts: 100% land_value NULL, 100% land_acres = 0.0000 (a written zero, not NULL), 100% property_use_code NULL, 271,164 (96%) DO have a positive market_value. 319,481 non-R-prefix accounts: land_value NULL on only 1 row (essentially fully populated).
williamson_48491.provenanceFinding: All 282,569 R-prefix rows carry source_file='stratmap25-landparcels_48491_lp.zip' (ingested 2026-08-25, matching the P-78 'leftover farm' StratMap Path-B greenfield pattern in _scratch/parcel-facts-write-path.md). The 319,466 real numeric-prop_id accounts instead carry source_file='property.csv' (WCAD's actual tax-roll export) or the WCAD Socrata portal pull. The R-prefix rows were never part of Williamson's real CAD-roll ingestion at all — they are a geometry-driven identity/shell fill from a different, later pipeline.
williamson_48491.realDataFound: This store already holds a genuine, richer WCAD-specific staging table — `tx_wcad_ag_valuation` (per-property land-segment detail: land_type, acres, value, curr_value, keyed by the SAME prop_id), acquired 2026-09-03 (11 days AFTER the 2026-08-25 leftover-farm fill). Sample: prop_id R349307 has a real land_type='L' row with acres=1.021, value=306 in tx_wcad_ag_valuation, while cad_property shows land_acres=0.0000 / land_value=NULL for that exact same prop_id. 299,712 of the table's 305,879 rows join to an R-prefix cad_property row on prop_id.
williamson_48491.mechanism: Two independently-run acquisition pipelines produced two different records for the same R-prefix parcels: the generic statewide leftover-farm StratMap fill (2026-08-25, placeholder land_acres=0/land_value=null) and a genuine per-property WCAD land-valuation detail pull (2026-09-03, real acres/value per land segment). The richer, later table was never reconciled back into cad_property.
williamson_48491.rejectedAlternative: Considered: WCAD's own accounting convention puts land value on a numeric 'parent' sibling account and R-prefix rows are genuinely land-value-free (matching the existing test fixture comment 'identity join hits R-prefix; dollars live on numeric'). Rejected: stripping the R-prefix / leading zeros from a sample of R-prefix prop_ids found ZERO matching numeric sibling rows in cad_property, and tx_wcad_ag_valuation's own land_type='L' rows carry real non-zero acres/value under the exact same R-prefixed prop_id — so the real land data is not missing, it is just staged in a different, unreconciled table.

mclennan_48309.verdict: REAL INGEST/PARSING GAP, not a legitimate absence. Different mechanism from Williamson.
mclennan_48309.liveQuery: WITH latest AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (prop_id) * FROM cad_property WHERE county_fips='48309' ORDER BY prop_id, tax_year DESC) SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE land_acres IS NULL), count(*) FILTER (WHERE land_value IS NOT NULL AND land_value>0) FROM latest;
mclennan_48309.measured: 114,255 total accounts, land_acres NULL on 100% (114,255/114,255), land_value present and positive on 113,322 (99%). All 114,255 rows share ONE source_file: stratmap25-landparcels_48309_lp.zip / source_vintage stratmap25-landparcels_48309_mclennan_202503 — this is McLennan's entire cad_property population, not a minority patch layer (unlike Williamson's R-prefix subset).
mclennan_48309.priorEstablishedContext: _inbox/2026-09-01_parcel-fill-48309_close.json already ruled 'McLennan assessed and living are null at the CAD authority; filling them would invent values' for assessed_value/living_area_sqft specifically — that is an accepted, prior-investigated genuine absence for THOSE two fields. This investigation is about a DIFFERENT field (land_acres) and found a different answer for it.
mclennan_48309.realDataFound: legal_description contains a parseable acreage figure on 110,358 of 114,255 rows (96.6%) via a regex match on 'Acres <number>'; the remaining rows mostly use a 'Total <number> Ac' phrasing the regex missed but which is still present as text (spot-checked 5 examples, e.g. 'AXTELL OT Block 5 Lot 4 5 & 0.116 Ac Aband ROW (A) Total 0.414 Ac'). No separate McLennan-specific staging table exists in this store (searched information_schema for any tx_mcad_*/mclennan_* table — none found), so unlike Williamson there is no already-staged structured source to reconcile from; the acreage exists only as embedded free text on the row itself.
mclennan_48309.mechanism: The loader that populated cad_property from this county's StratMap-format land-parcels drop extracts land_value/market_value correctly but never parses the acreage figure embedded in legal_description into the structured land_acres column, for any of the 114,255 rows in the county.
mclennan_48309.rejectedAlternative: Considered: McLennan's real CAD source (per OPS-1_texas_source_registry.md, McLennanCADWebService/FeatureServer via vendor bis-consultants) genuinely never carries a discrete acres field, matching the already-accepted assessed_value/living_area absence. Rejected: land_value and market_value ARE populated on 99% of rows from this same load — a purely geometry/GIS-oriented or field-poor source would not carry those either — and the acreage is visibly present as parseable text on the same rows that are missing the structured field, which points to a parsing gap in this specific loader rather than a genuinely field-poor source.

b3geomgapPredicateVerdict: B3-GEOMGAP's `land_acres>0 AND land_value>0` predicate is not the wrong check for either county — it is correctly finding that cad_property's stored data can't support the undivided-interest sweep for these two counties, because cad_property itself is missing real data that already exists (Williamson, in a staged sibling table) or is recoverable (McLennan, by parsing legal_description). Both counties' 'vacuous 0' should be treated as NOT YET MEASURABLE, not as a confirmed zero gap and not as something to patch by loosening the sweep's predicate.
recommendedNextStep: Not implemented here — this is a hauska-factory / CAD-ingest-pipeline fix, outside the ctx-wrapup-engine lane's repo (hauska-engine only reads whatever cad_property already contains; ingest-existing.ts is behaving correctly given its inputs). Two distinct, separately-scoped fixes needed: (1) Williamson — reconcile tx_wcad_ag_valuation's land_type-segment rows into cad_property.land_value/land_acres for the 282,569 R-prefix accounts (aggregate per prop_id; land_type coding needs a real key, e.g. 'L' rows look like the land segment, but the other 26 land_type codes in that table were not characterized here and should be before writing an aggregation rule). (2) McLennan — add legal_description acreage parsing to whatever loader processes this county's StratMap-format drop, or re-source from McLennanCADWebService directly if that is judged more reliable than text-mining legal_description. Both need their own scoping/dispatch, not a blanket fix.
toolsAndAccess: gcloud (existing session auth, project hauska-prod-497015) to fetch CORTEX_DATABASE_URL from Secret Manager; psql (existing PostgreSQL 18 client tools install) for all queries.
